data.narrative:
Tokamak Energy, a Series C nuclear energy company founded by David Kingham, Mikhail Gryaznevich, and Alan Sykes, has raised $335M+ to date. The broader nuclear energy sector comprises 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private companies including Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, and Fuse Energy.

Stage-progression methodology applies here, using the $335M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the next funding stage, yielding $570M. A peer-median approach is not applicable; while 5 same-sector peers exist, insufficient overlap occurs in stage, valuation tier, or comparable metrics—only 1 adjacent-stage comparable could be identified—falling short of the three-point minimum needed for reliable triangulation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $484M to $655M, centered on $570M. This single-method conclusion carries material uncertainty. The low-to-high range reflects bounds around the stage-progression result rather than cross-validation against market comparables. Key uncertainties include the lack of direct peer benchmarking in this nascent subsector, the wide heterogeneity among nuclear energy approaches, and limited public trading data for nascent technology companies. Any valuation above this range would require either material operational de-risking or external market data not present in the current dataset.
